name: Alexander Hamilton
role: First U.S. Secretary of the Treasury (1789-1795) and Federalist leader
summary: Hamilton argued for a strong national government with an energetic executive, an independent judiciary and a Senate and executive serving long terms. As Treasury Secretary he funded the national debt, founded a national bank on implied powers, and urged protective duties and bounties for manufactures. He opposed slavery, helped found the New York Manumission Society and welcomed immigration, while distrusting democratic excess and favoring British-style stability.

notes: Born 1755 or 1757. Second pass (claude-opus-5-5, 2026-11-07): read his own texts in full in the Lodge Federal Edition (archive.org scans, vols. 1-10, kept in scratchpad/sources/alexander-hamilton/) and the Gutenberg J. C. Hamilton vol. 1, plus Treasury and Federal Reserve History pages for the Treasury record. Founders Online refused scripted access (AWS WAF bot challenge), so it was not used. Searched every theme: economy (bank, public credit, loans, manufactures, taxes), government (NY ratifying convention, 1787 draft constitution, Federalist, Virginia and Kentucky resolutions, secession), world (Pacificus, Quasi-War letters), society and culture (Examination of 1802 on immigrants, 1779 letter on Black soldiers), liberty (Phocion, Tully, Farmer Refuted). Answers that rested on Wikipedia were re-sourced to his own texts or nulled; where his Treasury or military record bears on a statement it answers alone. His view of immigration hardened by 1802 (Examination VIII), which made reduce-immigration mixed. The Farewell Address draft was not used: he wrote it in Washington's voice. Ecology and technology statements are anachronistic for him.
